body: Incidental s-risks arise when efficient ways to achieve a certain goal creates a lot of suffering in the process, without anyone actively trying to cause suffering per se. The agent or agents that cause the s-risk are either indifferent to that suffering, or they would prefer a suffering-free alternative in theory, but are not willing to bear the necessary costs in practice.
